docs.title: Welcome to my Homelab documentation
docs.text:
This documentation is where I track my infrastructure setup, how-to's, cheatsheet, experiments and automation projects. My lab runs primarily on a Proxmox cluster with TrueNAS SCALE for storage and Kubernetes (k3s) for running services. I use Ansible to automate deployments and manage various operational tasks. Additionally, I follow a GitOps approach for Kubernetes using a dedicated repository with ArgoCD to declaratively manage my services and configurations.

The goals of this documentation are twofold:

  • To serve as a reference for my own environment and workflows.
  • To share ideas, configurations, and lessons learned that may help others building or maintaining their own homelab.

Here, you’ll find notes, guides, and code snippets covering virtualization, storage, and automation, all tested and documented from a real-world setup.

docs.title: 3-2-1 Backup Strategy
docs.text: 3 Copies, 2 media volumes (truenas-a and truenas-b), 1 off-site (truenas-c)

docs.title: off-site
docs.text:
Off-site backup is a replication task from the truenas-master to truenas-c, it is connected via VPN using wireguard.

Configure wireguard connection after boot on truenas-c

  1. Create a wg0.conf in /data/wg0.conf only this directory is persistent.

  2. Add the following content (see bitwarden for full config including keys) 

     [Interface]
 PrivateKey = **removed**
 Address = 10.44.44.3/32
 DNS = 1.1.1.1

 [Peer]
 PublicKey = **removed**
 Endpoint = **removed**:51820
 AllowedIPs = 10.44.44.3/32,10.0.10.0/24,10.0.100.0/24,10.42.0.0/16
 PersistentKeepalive = 25

  3. Go to /ui/system/initshutdown and configure the init command as follow:

    • Type: Command
    • Description: wireguard up at boot
    • When: Post Init
    • Command/Script: /usr/bin/wg-quick up /data/wg0.conf
    • Enabled: Yes

docs.title: Resize VM disk
docs.text:
sudo dnf install cloud-utils-growpart

sudo growpart /dev/sda 2

sudo pvresize /dev/sda2

sudo lvextend -l +100%FREE /dev/mapper/rl-root

sudo xfs_growfs /

docs.title: Script
docs.text:
1. Run the following script to start a interactive script that repair the iSCSI share
curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/x-real-ip/infrastructure/refs/heads/main/scripts/repair_iscsi_volume.sh | bash

docs.title: Manually
docs.text:
1. Make sure that the container that uses the volume has stopped.

  2. SSH into one of the nodes in the cluster and start discovery

    sudo iscsiadm -m discovery -t st -p truenas-master.lan.stamx.nl && \
read -p "Enter the disk name: " DISKNAME && \
export DISKNAME

  3. Login to target

    sudo iscsiadm --mode node --targetname iqn.2005-10.org.freenas.ctl:${DISKNAME} --portal truenas-master.lan.stamx.nl --login && \
sleep 5 && \
lsblk && \
read -p "Enter the device ('sda' for example): " DEVICENAME && \
export DEVICENAME

  4. Create a local mount point & mount to replay logfile

    sudo mkdir -vp /mnt/data-0 && sudo mount /dev/${DEVICENAME} /mnt/data-0/

  5. Unmount the device

    sudo umount /mnt/data-0/

  6. Run check / ncheck

    sudo xfs_repair -n /dev/${DEVICENAME}; sudo xfs_ncheck /dev/${DEVICENAME}
echo "If filesystem corruption was corrected due to replay of the logfile, the xfs_ncheck should produce a list of nodes and pathnames, instead of the errorlog."

  7. If needed run xfs repair

    sudo xfs_repair /dev/${DEVICENAME}

  8. Logout from target

    sudo iscsiadm --mode node --targetname iqn.2005-10.org.freenas.ctl:${DISKNAME} --portal storage-server-lagg.lan.stamx.nl --logout
echo "Volumes are now ready to be mounted as PVCs."

docs.title: Rsync
docs.text:
Run a Rsync exact copy

sudo rsync -axHAWXS --numeric-ids --info=progress2 /mnt/sourcePart/ /mnt/destPart

docs.title: Bitnami Sealed Secret
docs.text:
Raw mode

echo -n foo | kubeseal --cert "./sealed-secret-tls-2.crt" --raw --scope cluster-wide

Create TLS (unencrypted) secret

kubectl create secret tls cloudflare-tls --key origin-ca.pk --cert origin-ca.crt --dry-run=client -o yaml > cloudflare-tls.yaml

Encrypt secret with custom public certificate.

kubeseal --cert "./sealed-secret-tls-2.crt" --format=yaml < secret.yaml > sealed-secret.yaml

Add sealed secret to configfile secret

echo -n <mypassword_value> | kubectl create secret generic <secretname> --dry-run=client --from-file=<password_key>=/dev/stdin -o json | kubeseal --cert ./sealed-secret-tls-2.crt -o yaml \
-n democratic-csi --merge-into <secret>.yaml

Raw sealed secret

strict scope (default):

echo -n foo | kubeseal --raw --from-file=/dev/stdin --namespace bar --name mysecret
AgBChHUWLMx...

With the custom cert (useful when patching just one key of an existing SealedSecret, e.g. via a kustomize JSON6902 patch on encryptedData.<KEY>):

echo -n foo | kubeseal --cert ./sealed-secret-tls-2.crt --raw --from-file=/dev/stdin --namespace bar --name mysecret
AgBChHUWLMx...

Without a local cert file, fetch it live from the in-cluster controller instead. In this cluster the controller service is named sealed-secrets in kube-system, not the kubeseal default sealed-secrets-controller, so the name/namespace flags are required:

echo -n foo | kubeseal --raw \
  --controller-name sealed-secrets \
  --controller-namespace kube-system \
  --namespace bar --name mysecret
AgBChHUWLMx...

namespace-wide scope:

echo -n foo | kubeseal --cert ./sealed-secret-tls-2.crt --raw --from-file=/dev/stdin --namespace bar --scope namespace-wide
AgAbbFNkM54...

cluster-wide scope:

echo -n foo | kubeseal --cert ./sealed-secret-tls-2.crt --raw --from-file=/dev/stdin --scope cluster-wide
AgAjLKpIYV+...

No --namespace/--name needed here — the ciphertext isn't bound to a specific namespace+name. But this only decrypts if the target SealedSecret actually carries the sealedsecrets.bitnami.com/cluster-wide: "true" annotation (see below); without it the controller expects strict-scope ciphertext and unsealing fails. Since cluster-wide ciphertext isn't bound to one Secret, avoid it for per-app values like a db password — stick to strict there.

Include the sealedsecrets.bitnami.com/namespace-wide annotation in the SealedSecret

metadata:
  annotations:
    sealedsecrets.bitnami.com/namespace-wide: "true"

Include the sealedsecrets.bitnami.com/cluster-wide annotation in the SealedSecret

metadata:
  annotations:
    sealedsecrets.bitnami.com/cluster-wide: "true"

docs.title: Kubernetes
docs.text:
Drain and terminate all pods gracefully on the node while marking the node as unschedulable

kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data <nodename>

Make the node unschedulable

kubectl cordon <nodename>

Make the node schedulable

kubectl uncordon <nodename>

Convert to BASE64

echo -n '<value>' | base64

Decode a secret with config file data

kubectl get secret <secret_name> -o jsonpath='{.data}' -n <namespace>

Create secret from file

kubectl create secret generic <secret name> --from-file=<secret filelocation> --dry-run=client  --output=yaml > secrets.yaml

Restart Pod

kubectl rollout restart deployment <deployment name> -n <namespace>

Change PV reclaim policy

kubectl patch pv <pv-name> -p "{\"spec\":{\"persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy\":\"Retain\"}}"

Shell into pod

kubectl exec -it <pod_name> -- /bin/bash

Copy to or from pod

kubectl cp <namespace>/<pod>:/tmp/foo /tmp/bar

docs.title: Sudo
docs.text:
1. Install sudo

    apt update && apt install sudo
    2. Add user to sudoers group 
    sudo visudo
    3. Add the following line at the end of the file to grant coen user sudo privileges:

docs.text: Run the Ansible playbook setup the desktop desired state, see Infrastructure as Code page.

docs.title: Install Proxmox
docs.text: These steps (re)install one node or the whole cluster. Everything the Proxmox API can configure is managed by OpenTofu in the infrastructure repository. The steps below are the manual work before and after tofu apply.

docs.title: 1. Installer
docs.text:
Use the graphical installer and enter the following values.

pve-apve-b Setting Value Target disk Force MP500 (112 GB NVMe) Filesystem ext4 Advanced LVM options swapsize = 8, maxvz = 0 Hostname (FQDN) pve-a.lan.stamx.nl Management interface Onboard NIC Pin interface names Enabled (nic0, nic1, nic2) IP address (CIDR) 10.0.99.2/24 Gateway 10.0.99.1 DNS server 10.0.99.1 Setting Value Target disk KINGSTON SUV400S37240G (240 GB SATA) Filesystem ext4 Advanced LVM options swapsize = 8, maxvz = 0 Hostname (FQDN) pve-b.lan.stamx.nl Management interface Onboard NIC Pin interface names Enabled (nic0, nic1, nic2) IP address (CIDR) 10.0.99.3/24 Gateway 10.0.99.1 DNS server 10.0.99.1

Warning

Only select the boot disk. The other NVMe holds the vm-storage ZFS pool with the VM disks and must not be touched by the installer.

Note

maxvz = 0 skips the data volume, so there is no local-lvm storage to remove afterwards. VM disks live on vm-storage.

Note

The OpenTofu stack expects the interface names nic0 (onboard), nic1 and nic2 (PCI card). If the installer does not offer interface pinning, run pve-network-interface-pinning generate after the installation and reboot.

docs.title: 2. Prepare each node
docs.text:
1. Add the Ansible SSH key. Run this from the desktop.

    ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/ansible.pub root@10.0.99.2

  2. Extend the root logical volume over the free space. The installer caps root at 96 GiB and leaves some space unallocated.

    lvextend -r -l +100%FREE pve/root

  3. Import the existing ZFS pool. Never create it, it holds the VM disks.

    zpool import -f vm-storage

docs.title: 3. Create the cluster
docs.text:
1. Create the cluster on pve-a.

    pvecm create pve-cluster

  2. Join pve-b. This asks for the root password of pve-a.

    pvecm add 10.0.99.2

Reinstalling a single node

The remaining node still knows the reinstalled node. Remove it there before joining, for example for pve-b:

pvecm delnode pve-b
rm -r /etc/pve/nodes/pve-b

docs.title: 4. Create the OpenTofu API token
docs.text:
Run this once on any cluster node, for example over SSH from the desktop, and store tofu@pve!provider=<value> in Bitwarden. The value is shown only once.

ssh root@10.0.99.2 'pveum user add tofu@pve --comment "OpenTofu" \
  && pveum aclmod / -user tofu@pve -role Administrator \
  && pveum user token add tofu@pve provider --privsep 0'

Note

Users, ACLs and tokens live in /etc/pve, which is replicated to every node in the cluster, so running this once is enough. Do it after creating the cluster: a joining node replaces its /etc/pve with the one from the cluster.

docs.title: 5. Create the node certificates
docs.text:
The web interface and API of every node use a certificate from the stamx CA. Skip this step when ~/certs/proxmox on the desktop already holds valid certificates.

Run this on the desktop, not on a node

The CA private key must never leave the desktop. OpenTofu reads the certificates from ~/certs/proxmox and uploads them to the nodes in the next step.

  1. Create the directory and go into it.

    mkdir -p ~/certs/proxmox && cd ~/certs/proxmox

  2. Copy the CA certificate from the ansible repository.

    cp ~/git-repositories/infrastructure/ansible/roles/ca_trust/files/stamx-ca-certificate.crt ca.crt

  3. Create a private key and a certificate request for every node.

    pve-apve-b 
    openssl req -new -newkey rsa:4096 -nodes -keyout pve-a.key -out pve-a.csr \
  -subj "/O=stamx/CN=pve-a.lan.stamx.nl" \
  -addext "subjectAltName=DNS:pve-a.lan.stamx.nl,DNS:pve-a,IP:10.0.99.2" \
  -addext "basicConstraints=CA:FALSE" \
  -addext "keyUsage=critical,digitalSignature,keyEncipherment" \
  -addext "extendedKeyUsage=serverAuth"

    openssl req -new -newkey rsa:4096 -nodes -keyout pve-b.key -out pve-b.csr \
  -subj "/O=stamx/CN=pve-b.lan.stamx.nl" \
  -addext "subjectAltName=DNS:pve-b.lan.stamx.nl,DNS:pve-b,IP:10.0.99.3" \
  -addext "basicConstraints=CA:FALSE" \
  -addext "keyUsage=critical,digitalSignature,keyEncipherment" \
  -addext "extendedKeyUsage=serverAuth"

  4. Sign the requests with the CA. Replace /path/to/stamx-ca-private.key with the location of the CA private key.

    pve-apve-b 
    openssl x509 -req -in pve-a.csr -CA ca.crt -CAkey /path/to/stamx-ca-private.key \
  -CAcreateserial -copy_extensions copyall -days 825 -sha256 -out pve-a.crt

    openssl x509 -req -in pve-b.csr -CA ca.crt -CAkey /path/to/stamx-ca-private.key \
  -CAcreateserial -copy_extensions copyall -days 825 -sha256 -out pve-b.crt

  5. Check the certificates. Both must report OK.

    openssl verify -CAfile ca.crt pve-a.crt pve-b.crt

  6. Remove the requests and protect the private keys.

    rm pve-a.csr pve-b.csr && chmod 600 pve-a.key pve-b.key

Note

The certificates are valid for 825 days. To renew them, repeat this step and run tofu apply.

docs.title: 6. Apply OpenTofu
docs.text:
Apply the proxmox stack, see OpenTofu usage.

This configures the APT repositories (enterprise off, no-subscription on), DNS, /etc/hosts, the time zone, the bridges vmbr1 (wan) and vmbr2 (lan), the SDN VLANs, the vm-storage storage, the lsi-hba PCI mapping, the pools, the node certificates and the cluster options. The installer only creates vmbr0.

The state in git still knows the resources from before the reinstall, so OpenTofu only creates what is missing.

Reinstalling the whole cluster

HA, storage replication and pool membership refer to guests. After a reinstall of both nodes those guests do not exist yet, so leave them out of the first apply:

tofu apply \
  -exclude=proxmox_haresource.opnsense \
  -exclude=proxmox_replication.guest \
  -exclude=proxmox_pool_membership.guest

Run a plain tofu apply once the guests are back. Reinstalling a single node does not need this, because the guests keep running on the other node.

docs.title: 7. Finish each node
docs.text:
1. Update the system. This needs the no-subscription repository from the previous step.

    apt update && apt dist-upgrade -y

  2. Enable Wake-on-LAN on the onboard NIC. Add the up line to the nic0 stanza in /etc/network/interfaces.

    auto nic0
iface nic0 inet manual
    up /sbin/ethtool -s nic0 wol g

  3. Run the 'Proxmox VE CPU Scaling Governor' script and set it to powersave.

  4. Add the QDevice.

  5. Set up two-factor authentication for root via Datacenter -> Permissions -> Two Factor.

docs.title: On the Qdevice
docs.text:
1. This command sets the root password, enables root login in the SSH configuration, and restarts the SSH service.

    passwd root && sed -i 's/#PermitRootLogin/PermitRootLogin yes/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && systemctl restart sshd

  2. Install corosync packages

    apt install corosync-qnetd corosync-qdevice

docs.title: Make a VM HA
docs.text:
HA and storage replication are managed by OpenTofu in opentofu/stacks/proxmox/ha.tf. Changes made in the web interface are not in the code and get lost on a reinstall.

  1. Add the guest to replicated_guests in locals.tf, so its disks are replicated to pve-b every 15 minutes.
  2. Add a proxmox_haresource for the guest to ha.tf, and add it to the resources of a HA rule if it should prefer a node.
  3. Apply OpenTofu.

docs.text:
1. Find the USB stick device 

    lsblk

  2. Create mount directory 

    mkdir -p /mnt/pve/backup_usb-stick

  3. Mount (change <sd?> to the correct device) 

    mount /dev/<sd?> /mnt/pve/backup_usb-stick

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Remove old Debian package

    sudo apt remove ansible -y
    2. Install pipx

    sudo apt update
sudo apt install pipx
pipx ensurepath

  2. Install the minimal ansible-core package using pipx

    pipx install ansible-core

  3. Clone the infrastructure repository and go into the ansible directory 

     git clone https://github.com/x-real-ip/infrastructure.git
 cd infrastructure/ansible

  4. Install collections from the requirements.yaml located in the Ansible dir (optional)

    ansible-galaxy collection install -r requirements.yaml

    requirements.yaml example

    collections:
  - name: ansible.posix
  - name: kubernetes.core
  - name: community.general

docs.title: OpenTofu
docs.text:
The configuration of the infrastructure itself lives in the opentofu directory of the infrastructure repository. Every directory under opentofu/stacks has its own state and is planned and applied on its own.

Stack Manages proxmox Proxmox cluster, see Hypervisor

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: The desktop playbook installs OpenTofu from its APT repository and adds the stamx CA to the trust store.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
Both are stored in Bitwarden and only ever passed as environment variables.

Environment variable Contents TF_VAR_state_passphrase Passphrase that encrypts the state in git, at least 16 characters. Without it the state cannot be read. PROXMOX_VE_API_TOKEN tofu@pve!provider=<value>, see Create the OpenTofu API token.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
1. Go to the stack and export the secrets. Use single quotes, because the token contains a !. A leading space keeps the line out of the shell history.

    cd opentofu/stacks/proxmox
 export TF_VAR_state_passphrase='...'
 export PROXMOX_VE_API_TOKEN='tofu@pve!provider=...'

  2. Review the plan and apply it.

    tofu init
tofu plan
tofu apply

  3. Commit the updated terraform.tfstate. It is encrypted.

docs.title: Adopt existing resources
docs.text: To bring something that already exists under OpenTofu, add a temporary imports.tf with an import block for it. The plan must report only imports and no changes; if it shows a change, align the code with reality first. Remove imports.tf after the apply.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ansible installed on your local machine. See Infrastructure as Code page.
  • SSH access to the target machines where you want to install k3s.

docs.title: Add SSH keys on local device
docs.text:
1. Copy private and public key (stored in Bitwarden Vault)

    cp /path/to/my/key/ansible ~/.ssh/ansible
cp /path/to/my/key/ansible.pub ~/.ssh/ansible.pub

  2. Change permissions on the files

    sudo chmod 600 ~/.ssh/ansible
sudo chmod 600 ~/.ssh/ansible.pub

  3. Make ssh agent to actually use copied key

    ssh-add ~/.ssh/ansible

docs.title: Setting up VM hosts on Proxmox
docs.text:
1. Create a VM with the following partitions
    • / (10 GB) xfs
    • /var (50GB) xfs
    • /boot (1GB)

Note

No swap partition is needed for kubernetes

  1. Login to the VM and set hostname. 
    hostnamectl set-hostname <hostname>
  2. Reboot.

  3. Set static ip for the VM in the DHCP server.

  4. Reboot.

  5. Set this hostname in the ansible inventory hosts.yaml file.

docs.title: VLAN's
docs.text:

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Download the minimal .xz-compressed image file from https://fi.mirror.armbian.de/archive/odroidc4/archive/
  2. Write the .xz compressed image with balenaEtcher
  3. Insert the SD/MMC and boot
  4. Login via SSH user root default password 1234
